title: Variadic Average
hints: Inside the function, a variadic `Double...` parameter is just a `[Double]`.
Put the real work in an array-taking overload and have the variadic version forward to it.
`func average(_ numbers: Double...) -> Double? { average(of: numbers) }`, with `numbers.isEmpty ? nil : sum / Double(count)`.
jsBridge: Like JS rest parameters (`...numbers`), but you can't spread an array into a Swift variadic parameter; there's no `average(...arr)`. That's why APIs provide an array overload too.

compass.q: JS `fn(...arr)` spreads an array. Swift has no splat. What design pattern does that force on API authors?
Can a function have two variadic parameters? (Swift 5.4 changed this.) What disambiguates them?
Variadic vs `[Double]` parameter: which is nicer at the call site, and which is more flexible?
`print(_ items: Any...)` is variadic. What does `Any...` cost in type safety?

videos.title: Variadic functions – Swift in Sixty Seconds
videos.moment: Some functions are variadic, which is a fancy way of saying they accept any number of parameters of the same type.
